rules.statement: V was an Arasaka corporate employee in Arthur Jenkins' department (the Corporate lifepath): V had the private meeting in Jenkins' office in The Corpo-Rat and he treated V as one of his people.
In the Arasaka lobby V and Frank Nostra had a full catch-up: V asked about the Cape Town op, what people said about Jenkins, and who Frank worked under (Abernathy).

In his office Jenkins gave V a datashard with everything he had collected on Director Abernathy and a payment, telling V to make sure she was no longer a problem, with unaffiliated hires and someone V knew well for the core task. V took both.
V is not an Arasaka corporate: V never worked at Arasaka or in Jenkins' department, so V has no office history or friendship with Jenkins, Frank Nostra or their colleagues.

At Embers Hanako offered to lead V to Mikoshi beneath Arasaka Tower, in return for V testifying against her brother Yorinobu at the board meeting she would get V into. This records the offer only, not V's acceptance.
V went to Hanako's estate with Hellman; Takemura had been lost at the safe house and took no part in the estate rescue.
Evelyn privately offered V a fifty percent cut if V cut fixer Dex out of the job, and V answered "I'll think about it" instead of refusing outright.
After the Heist V had Jackie's body delivered to Viktor Vektor's clinic; Delamain confirmed the delivery.
In The Pickup V and Jackie found Brick, whom Royce had imprisoned rigged to a mine, and V disarmed the charge and freed him.
After the All Foods job V confronted Anthony Gilchrist with Jackie present, telling him V had seen the LOA-stamped manifests and knew he was the mole.
At the end of The Pickup V told Meredith Stout who the mole was: the cargo manifests stamped LOA pointed to her colleague Anthony Gilchrist.
Before the All Foods job V met Militech agent Meredith Stout, who questioned V about the missing convoy and about the mole Anthony Gilchrist.

At Batty's hotel Placide briefed V as the outside operative for the Grand Imperial Mall job: sync with the Voodoo Boys' subnet, find his people near the mall, and Brigitte could then solve V's problem.
After the Grand Imperial Mall job V came back alive to Batty's hotel and confronted Placide there about what had happened.

In The Ride Dex briefed V and Jackie on the job: steal an Arasaka prototype biochip for client Evelyn Parker, which first needs the Flathead combat bot Dex bought from Maelstrom's Brick, whom Royce had since replaced.
After V replied to her message, Meredith Stout texted V an invitation: No-Tell Motel, first floor, come alone.
V took Stout up on her invitation and came to the No-Tell Motel, where she was waiting. This records only that V showed up.
At the Totentanz V and Nancy met Brick, who had taken over the Maelstrom gang from Royce after the All Foods incident.
At the Totentanz V and Nancy were received by Patricia and her Maelstrom crew, not by Brick.
At the Totentanz V and Nancy dealt with Royce and Dum Dum, who were still running the Maelstrom gang there.
At the Arasaka board meeting in the tower V gave testimony; Yorinobu's armed forces then attacked and V fought them off.
In Arasaka Tower, Hanako took V to Saburo Arasaka's engram in Mikoshi ("Father. It is he.") and V spoke with it before the board meeting.
On the CEO floor V confronted Yorinobu Arasaka, who explained why he opposed Saburo's rule by fear; V held him unharmed until Hanako arrived and took charge of him.
On the CEO floor V reached Yorinobu without harming him, as Hanako had asked, and held him until Hanako arrived and took charge of him.

In War Pigs V went to the briefcase location and met Frank Nostra there. Purged by Abernathy, he held V at gunpoint to win his way back; V confronted him. This does not record how the confrontation ended.

The current save establishes that V and Johnny made contact with Alt beyond the Blackwall. Alt discussed a route into Mikoshi and supplied a way to contact her. This does not establish that Hanako, Placide, or another outsider witnessed it, nor any later ending outcome. V has disclosed this history to the present listener.

V accepted Meredith Stout’s Militech credchip at their initial meeting. Its malware was still present at handover; this history says nothing about later cleaning, copying, payment, or who won the Militech investigation.
V declined or abandoned Meredith Stout’s credchip offer at the initial meeting. No particular spoken refusal, later factory payment, or winner of the Militech investigation follows from that.

V refused to sign the Secure Your Soul contract in the Arasaka orbital clinic and chose to return to Earth. This does not establish a later cure, date of death, or another ending. V has disclosed this decision to the present listener.

V signed the Secure Your Soul contract in the Arasaka orbital clinic, agreeing to digitization and storage while awaiting a suitable body. No future restoration or cure is established. V has disclosed this decision to the present listener.

The current save establishes that V accepted the NetWatch agent’s arrangement in the Grand Imperial Mall: let the agent leave with his data in exchange for removing the Voodoo Boys’ virus and releasing their trapped netrunners. Those were the offered terms, not a guarantee of later safety. V has disclosed this private history to the present listener.

The NetWatch agent warned V about the Voodoo Boys’ malware and demonstrated that V’s diagnostic was repeating a forged result. This does not establish whether V accepted the NetWatch bargain. V has disclosed the warning to the present listener.
V and Meredith Stout completed their private motel encounter. It was an optional intimate meeting; it does not establish an ongoing romance, exclusivity, or a promise of another meeting.

rules.statement: When V asked Carol to help hack MaxTac for the convoy job she refused because of the risk to the Aldecaldos, but then messaged V to offer a gift in its place.
When V called Panam from the cabin in the Devil ending, V had never been her lover, and she answered warmly: "it's been a while since I heard that voice."
V went with Mitch to the bridge and shared the send-off for Scorpion in I'll Fly Away, completing it with him.
V did not see Mitch's farewell for Scorpion through: I'll Fly Away was abandoned and failed, so V was not with him at the bridge.
V delivered Jake's implant to Bob and warned him it carried a virus (the police sabotage), so it had to be re-flashed from the original firmware shard. Bob thanked V for being careful.
V agreed to help Bob's family in Fortunate Son and took on the errand of meeting the hospital contact in Little China to fetch Jake's kidney implant.
When V asked after Jake, Bob said the implant had taken and Jake was easing into it slowly, needing a day or two to get back on his feet.
On the Bruce Welby rescue V killed none of the guards or workers, so Dakota's no-unnecessary-bloodshed condition was met when she closed the gig.
On the Bruce Welby rescue V killed at least one guard or worker, breaking Dakota's no-unnecessary-bloodshed condition; her debrief reminded V she had said so.
Bruce Welby, rescued in Dakota's Goodbye, Night City gig, was among the Aldecaldos at the camp party and spoke of settling there.
V walked away from the Gun Music deal and the quest failed. Carol messaged V that the Aldecaldos had put their hopes on V and she would let it slide this time only because Panam sees something in V.
The Gun Music deal broke down into a firefight and V defeated the scavengers.
At the Gun Music scav deal V threatened the scav leader by pointing to V's implants, and he told his people to hand over the eddies, so the deal went through without a firefight.

After Riders on the Storm Cassidy texted V that she and the nomads had seen V and Panam getting along and hoped it worked out, adding a joking threat to hang V by the tonsils if it failed through V's fault.
After the No Fixers gig Iris Tanner texted V to thank V for handling her ride, saying she had left a small token at the drop point by the Sunset Motel, which made them even.
Dakota messaged V that her last contract was done, thanked V, and said a parting gift was already waiting in the garage.

After V's body was left to Johnny in the Temperance ending, Panam sent V a string of angry texts, one calling Johnny a sociopath and vowing to find him and get V back. These record her messages and suspicion, not that she saw what happened.

Dakota set up a shielded rig for V's Net run to meet Alt while Carol watched over V. Afterward Dakota's equipment was fried and Carol checked on V after a sharp neural spike. Neither heard what V and Alt discussed.
Bruce Welby, whom V rescued in Dakota's gig, was at the Aldecaldo party and told V he might make the camp his home.
Jake was at the Aldecaldo party after V's initiation, up and playing music after the transplant V delivered.
In Cassidy's bottle-shooting contest at the Aldecaldo party V hit at least eleven bottles (the game's pass line), so Cassidy praised the shooting and offered V her revolver.
While chasing Hellman after the AV crash, V and Panam followed physical evidence: V scanned the tire tracks at the crash site to trace where Hellman was taken.
At the convoy before the crossing Kerry told V he could not leave Night City yet, still had business there, and asked V to look him up if V ever came back through.
At the convoy before the crossing River told V he was staying in Night City to take care of his family and could not go with the nomads.
The Militech convoy operation brought a Basilisk back to the Aldecaldo camp. Panam presented it to Saul and the clan kept it for assembly.
Dakota's Flying Drugs contract was completed: the interference antenna was disabled, clearing the obstruction to the smuggling drones.
Benedict McAdams was extracted and delivered to his nomad contact, completing Dakota's MIA contract.
Bruce was rescued from the detention camp and handed over to Archibald, completing Dakota's Goodbye, Night City contract.
Iris Tanner was rescued for Dakota's No Fixers contract, and Iris's van was delivered as well.
V completed Dakota's Dancing on a Minefield job and delivered the recovered vehicle from the minefield.
The mobile Militech radar prototype was brought to Dakota's workshop, and the Radar Love contract was completed.
The requested training software was delivered for Dakota's Sparring Partner contract.
Trevor's remains were recovered and handed over through Dakota's arranged transport, completing Trevor's Last Ride.

While sheltering after his rescue, V defended Saul's practical case for accepting corporate support to help the clan survive. Saul approved the reasoning and Panam objected. This was a position in that conversation, not permanent hostility toward Panam or proof that the Biotechnica agreement later continued.

While sheltering after Saul's rescue, V initially backed Panam's criticism of Saul's corporate-dependence plan. Panam thanked V and Saul challenged the opinion. This records that initial stance, not which later explanation V gave or a permanent allegiance.
Carol sent V a message saying she had arranged a small gift by courier, with a drop on Potomac Street. This establishes her offer and dispatch message, not that V read it or collected the gift.
V accepted Panam's invitation to share an intimate experience through the Basilisk's sensory link, and the two became lovers.

After rescuing Saul, V made a flirtatious overture during the private farmhouse conversation with Panam. The established choice does not distinguish the physical-touch option from gentler banter and does not establish sex, mutual romantic commitment, or permission to ignore her boundaries.

At the Sunset Motel after Ghost Town, V made clear that the shared-room suggestion was flirtatious. Panam said she was glad they had met but was too tired for intimacy that night. This early exchange did not establish a committed relationship.
After the Ghost Town job, V and Panam shared a Sunset Motel room with separate twin beds and settled down for the night. Sharing the room was not a sexual encounter or a confirmed romance.

V agreed to help Panam pursue Nash after recovering her vehicle and cargo, and joined her raid at the Raffen tunnel hideout. Their tunnel encounter was completed. This does not establish that V killed Nash or that Panam and V became romantic partners.
V told Saul that Panam and the veterans planned to steal a Militech Basilisk convoy behind his back. Saul learned the plan from V.
V explained to Panam that a biochip and the personality construct inside it are harming V and threatening V's life. Panam knows this is why V is trying to survive.
After the camp was saved, Saul announced that Panam would lead the Aldecaldo family alongside him. Panam became his co-leader.
V helped free Saul from the Raffen Shiv. The rescue and escape through the storm were completed, and Saul survived to shelter at the farmhouse.
During the Aldecaldo assault inside Arasaka, Adam Smasher killed Saul in front of V and Panam. Panam witnessed Saul's death.
Saul and Panam formally welcomed V into the Aldecaldos. V received the clan jacket as a member of the family before the assault.

Mama Welles held Jackie's ofrenda at El Coyote Cojo, and V took part through the ceremony and toast.
V reminded Mama Welles how important Misty was to Jackie and encouraged Mama to invite Misty to dinner.
V disclosed the following save-established instruction: V asked Delamain to take Jackie's remains to his family, and Delamain identified Mama Welles as the recipient.

V disclosed the following save-established instruction: V asked Delamain to take Jackie's remains to Viktor's clinic. This instruction alone does not establish what happened to the body at the clinic.

V disclosed the following save-established instruction: V initially asked Delamain to wait at the No-Tell Motel with Jackie's remains. This instruction alone does not state the later delivery destination.
Jesse recovered sufficiently to call V, confirmed that he had transferred payment for the help, and thanked V.
rules.notes: Disabled 2026-10-05: its only predicate is whole-quest completion of mq012_stud, which also completes on the dead-passenger route, so it could tell a dead Jesse that he called and paid V.

rules.statement: V agreed to help Jesse reach a ripperdoc during his implant emergency.
Nix recovered from the dangerous deck decryption after V breached the system and preserved its data. Nix and V discussed the rescue afterward.
Nix recovered after V cut the power during the dangerous deck decryption; their recovery conversation established that the deck's data was wiped.
V delivered the old spellbook tablet to Nix and completed its sale. The agreed payment amount is not established by this observation.
Pepe later messaged V that, despite not knowing everything about Cynthia's past, he knew she loved him and was choosing their marriage.
Pepe later messaged V that Cynthia was no longer in his home and that he no longer trusted her. This establishes their separation, not which particular earlier advice V selected.
V told Pepe what Cynthia had explained, urged him to recognize that she loved him, and advised him to forgive the concealed appearance change. Pepe accepted that advice during their conversation.
Wilson's shooting competition recorded V in first place. Wilson judged the contest.
Wilson's shooting competition recorded Rudy in first place and V in second. Wilson judged the contest.
V beat Buck in the Arroyo Beat on the Brat fight; Fred texted that word on the street was that Buck needed new teeth.
V accepted Fred's offer to throw the Razor Hughes finale and then lost it; afterwards Fred said the loss looked natural and Viktor said V had thrown the fight.
V beat Cesar in the Glen Beat on the Brat fight; Fred texted about it (one variant adds that Cesar was allowed to keep his money).
V beat the Kabuki twins in the Beat on the Brat fight; Fred texted afterwards that he had heard V whooped the twin freaks.
V beat Rhino in the sanctioned Beat on the Brat bout at the Animals' club; Fred texted congratulations.
The Rancho Coronado Beat on the Brat qualifier was closed through open combat at the Animals' club rather than the sanctioned bout; Fred texted that he heard things got ugly there.
Before the Razor Hughes finale Viktor told V that Razor had a weakness: abdominal muscles that had been swapped out, so V should hit him there.
After V's attempt to help Aaron, Fred texted that it was a shame what happened to Aaron but he knew the risk; this is the game's Aaron-dead variant of Fred's report and he thanks V for trying.
After V's dealings with Angie, Fred texted that he did not know exactly what happened but Aaron would waste away with the Animals; he had hoped Aaron could be helped.
Fred sent V a message asking her/him to talk to his boxer friend Aaron and help him (No Easy Way Out).
Instead of the full ofrenda route, Mama Welles messaged V that she had found something that belonged to Jackie and left it for V in front of V's apartment, and V collected the package.
V invited Misty to Jackie's ofrenda; she came, rode with V to the ceremony and was with Mama Welles and V at the ofrenda.
V had Jackie's body taken to Viktor's clinic; Arasaka agents then seized it there, forcing Viktor to the floor.
Over noodles at the megabuilding, Jackie told V he had landed them a job fronted by the fixer Dexter DeShawn, arranged through T-Bug, and that Dex wanted to meet V face to face.
V drove the distressed Jesse to the ripperdoc clinic and he arrived alive; V then waited for his call (Burning Desire).
V put the recovered Kold Mirage deck down on Nix's counter at the Afterlife so that he could begin decrypting it.
Nix messaged that he had what V asked for, then met V at the Arasaka Memorial and handed over the convoy data: itinerary, vehicle order, defenses and the detainee's details.

Viktor treated V at the clinic after V dragged in beaten and half-conscious, warned that V had reached a critical juncture and would flatline in some back alley after the next attack, and told V to take matters into his own hands.

When an Arasaka car arrived for V outside Misty's Esoterica, Misty recognised the stretch, objected that Arasaka had killed Jackie, and called V's decision to work with them a betrayal; V then left with Hellman and Takemura.
While V waited at Misty's Esoterica, Panam's car arrived for V; Misty saw it come and said goodbye as Panam took V to the Aldecaldo camp.
After Viktor's ultimatum, Misty led V up to the clinic rooftop where she goes to be alone with her thoughts, and V sat down beside her to think.
V drove Ozob Bozo to his destination, fought off the ambush on the way and finished the job by talking to Ozob afterwards (Send in the Clowns).
When two Valentino thugs threatened Pepe at the bar, V fought and beat them rather than talking them down.
At El Coyote Cojo Pepe told V he owed Kirk Sawyer money and was afraid of what Kirk would do; V agreed to talk to Kirk on his behalf.
Pepe hired V to follow his wife and check his suspicions, and V began the investigation by going to the area where she works.

Misty took V home after Viktor's clinic and explained the medicines: omega blockers to slow the Relic and keep Johnny quiet, and her own pseudoendotrizine to speed things up; she gave V a lucky charm Viktor pulled out of V's skull and urged V to sleep, and V took the pills.
After the Heist, Viktor told V that the biochip was a bomb with the fuse lit, that Silverhand's construct was overwriting V's consciousness, and that V had only a few weeks.
After finding all twenty city murals V returned to Misty, who told V the tarot said V would reach the World by one of four paths: the Sun, the Star, Temperance or the Devil.
At the end of that final tarot reading Misty gave V a dreamcatcher ("Take this. It's all I can do to help") and wished V luck on whatever road V chose.

After finding all four King murals in Dogtown, V went to Misty and asked what the four Kings meant; she said V was caught between strong, warring personalities who all wanted to influence V, and that V's fate was still V's to shape.
After spotting the first strange tarot mural, V showed Misty the scan; she said it was a major arcanum sign from a higher power and told V to keep looking for more images.
V told Viktor about the strange murals they kept seeing; he said it was probably the biochip overloading the brain and that the only fix was to get rid of the chip.

In 2079 Misty found V hurt in the alley, talked with V while her ride was on its way, and V walked her to it; she said "So, till we meet again, I guess" and that the pendant she once gave V no longer mattered.
In 2079, after waking from the coma, V called Viktor; he ended the call by saying he would see V at his clinic, "You know the address".
In 2079 Viktor scanned V in his clinic and found that V's cortex had turned deaf to implant signals; he could find no safe fix and admitted he had been wrong to promise one.

When V messaged Viktor about the identity problem, he replied that psychotherapy works best and the key is exposing the patient to something personal from their true reality; he also warned the patient is highly suggestible.
V took part in Robert Wilson's shooting contest at the gun range (Shoot to Thrill) and shot through the round.

Ana heard Katya describe Bana's capture and claim she had kept him alive before someone else killed him. Ana rejected the claim and ordered V to kill Katya and recover the biomonitor. The order does not prove V obeyed it, and Katya's account remains her allegation.
V left Bana's biomonitor with Ana. Ana intended to use it as evidence in a disclosure; receipt of the device does not establish the subsequent outcome.
Evelyn died, and Judy sent V a message reporting that she had buried her. This establishes Judy’s burial report to V; it does not establish that V read it or which support reply V chose.
V received Sampson's later message offering his repaired car in thanks for preventing Claire from killing him. This private message is available to Claire only after V actually tells her about it.

V agreed to keep driving for Claire with winning as the priority and refused to promise an execution of Sampson. Claire accepted that boundary at the time. This agreement does not establish what happened to Sampson in the final confrontation.
Claire's confrontation with Sampson after the final chase ended in his death. The resolved outcome does not establish which final dialogue V used or that V personally watched the shooting.
Claire ultimately spared Sampson after the final chase. V's intervention stopped her from killing him. This does not erase Dean's death or mean Claire's grief and anger are resolved.
V and Judy got Evelyn out of the scavenger braindance studio. This records her rescue at that point; her medical recovery and later fate are separate events.
V told Jefferson that Holt and SSI were involved in spying on him. Jefferson received this as V's report; the report does not independently establish the allegation's truth.
V disclosed to Jefferson that the operation involved altering his mind and was not simply Holt's spying. This does not establish who ultimately controlled it.
Randy survived the rescue at the farm. River was directly involved in finding and helping his nephew.
V and River reached Randy too late after the wrong-farm route; Randy did not survive. This does not establish that River later killed Harris.

V supported installing Maiko to run Clouds under its arrangement with the Tyger Claws. Judy confronted V about letting Maiko take control. This does not mean Clouds became permanently independent or that Judy approved of the compromise.

Maiko died in the Clouds confrontation, and Judy learned that V killed her. Judy was shocked and distressed. This records her response at the debrief; it does not establish her later relationship with V.

V accepted Maiko's money after supporting her takeover. Judy learned this in the debrief and treated it as a betrayal of what she wanted for Clouds; she withdrew from V rather than accepting the deal as a shared victory.

Judy and V completed the Laguna Bend dive, and Judy brought V out of the water after V lost consciousness. The shared dive does not establish romance, an overnight stay, or what they said in optional conversations.

V stayed overnight at Judy’s apartment and woke there. Judy sent V a morning message about the breakfast she had left. This establishes her overnight care, not whether V accepted her Clouds plan, ate breakfast, disclosed Johnny, or began a romance.

During the morning after their night together, V and River agreed to try a romantic relationship. This is their decision at that time, not proof that later events have left the relationship unchanged.

The save establishes that V acknowledged inspecting Sandra's databank when returning it. Sandra knows about that access; this does not establish which later response V chose or that she shared every technical detail.

V attempted to extort Sandra by threatening to expose the databank findings. Sandra responded with armed hostility. Hostility does not establish that Sandra died, and she has no reason to treat this as friendly cooperation.

Joss sent V a private message saying she had been told that River’s and Randy’s bodies were found at a farm. She blamed V for abandoning them and said she would not forgive it. This is her received report and reaction, not something she personally witnessed.

After V’s family visit and game with the children, Joss thanked V for stopping by and passed along the children’s greetings and wish for a rematch. Her hospitality does not establish a romance with River, the content of their private conversation, or V’s response to her matchmaking.

After Randy survived the rescue, Joss told V that he was gradually easing back into things. She expressed gratitude and hope that things would be all right. This is her follow-up assessment, not proof of complete medical recovery or a message V has read or answered.

After the failed rescue, River privately reported to V that he had killed Harris and covered his tracks. This is River’s account of what he did afterward; the message does not establish that V witnessed it or that Joss was told.
Johnny used V’s body for the night and handed control back after the outing.
V and Johnny completed the visit to Karim’s Samurai bootleg stall.
V arranged Johnny’s outing with Rogue; the pair subsequently met at the theater.
Johnny gained the Ebunike lead through Ruby and V later relayed it to Rogue.
V completed the Family Heirloom branch without returning Dan’s car.
V returned Dan’s car during Family Heirloom.
V delivered Dan’s recording for Nancy’s Family Heirloom job.
V cashed Kang Tao’s credchip and received the payment.
Karl Ginsky was killed during Nasty Hangover, and Rogue received the debrief.
Karl Ginsky survived and Rogue arranged a safehouse for him.
At Kerry’s villa, Kerry recognized Johnny speaking through V.
Johnny proposed bringing Samurai back during the meeting with Kerry; the performance had not happened yet.
V safely extracted Nancy from the Totentanz encounter.
V delivered Kerry’s stolen guitar to the gig’s drop point.
Rebeca Price was delivered alive, and Rogue acknowledged receiving her.
Rebeca Price was killed, and Rogue acknowledged the lethal result.
V paid Rogue, who supplied the Hellman lead and directed V to Panam.
V and Kerry completed the planned equipment sabotage.
Johnny selected the tattoo named “Johnny’s Special” during his night using V’s body.
Johnny selected the tattoo named “Together Forever” during his night using V’s body.
Royce’s group controlled the Totentanz encounter that V navigated with Nancy.
The gig’s debrief confirms that Vega died and nobody else was killed.
Vic Vega was delivered alive in the car for Rogue.
Vic Vega was killed, and Rogue received the lethal debrief.
V agreed to be Claire's driver in the NC underground racing circuit and drove her first qualifying race (City Center).
Claire texted V that she had left V the Beast, her prized car, because she would not need it anymore.
V won the final Big Race, crossing the finish line before any opponent.
During the final Big Race (The Beast in Me), V stayed on the race course and kept racing rather than following Sampson.
During the final Big Race (The Beast in Me), V left the race route to follow Sampson instead of continuing the race. The outcome of that chase is a separate matter.
Jefferson Peralez won the Night City mayoral election; N54 News announced it.
In a ramen shop Elizabeth Peralez privately confessed her fears to V and begged V never to let Jefferson find out, saying his life depended on it.
After the Dream On case Jefferson Peralez texted V that he was glad he had trusted his gut in hiring V and that, after the elections, he might have more work for V.
At dinner with River (Following the River), V turned down River's romantic advance and the two agreed to stay friends.
At the end of The Hunt, River told V that he meant to kill Anthony Harris, who was in a coma in police custody. This was only a stated intention, not an act.
In The Hunt, V worked out from what the braindance had shown that the farm was Edgewood Farm and rode there with River, instead of guessing between two farms.
In The Hunt, V voted to check Poppy Farm first; it was the wrong farm and River realised it on arrival.
While investigating Rhyne's death with River, V plugged into the tampered BD wreath, was hit by its attack, and told River that someone had spiked the BD and that it killed Rhyne.
In their apartment V reported to Jefferson and Elizabeth Peralez that Rhyne's death was an embarrassing accident at a sex club which the NCPD had covered up. V did not tell them it was a BD murder.
In their apartment V told Jefferson and Elizabeth Peralez that Weldon Holt was behind Rhyne's death, admitting there was no proof, only strong suspicions.
In their apartment V told Jefferson and Elizabeth Peralez that the case was too complex to draw conclusions yet, and gave them no findings.
River and V confronted Detective Harold Han about the cover-up of Rhyne's death; River told him he knew what he had done. This establishes Han's part in the concealment, not who ordered it.
On the rooftop before choosing how to face Arasaka, V called River and the two of them talked.
In a text after the Santo Domingo race, V told Claire to remember what she had promised; Claire answered that Sampson dies during the race and only then, with no killing in cold blood.
After the Santo Domingo race, V refused to help Claire go after Sampson and told her "I'm done"; Claire accepted that V was out of her racing team.
At the final hotel meeting V chose to destroy the biomonitor evidence instead of handing it to Ana, siding with Steven; Ana protested that she would not let it go.
At the Aldecaldo camp before the crossing, River told V he was staying in Night City to look after his family and would not go with V.
At their meeting Sandra Dorsett handed V a shard with the MaxTac convoy data she had gathered, and V took it.
After the MaxTac ambush V had uploaded Sandra Dorsett's virus with the Ping quickhack, and Sandra texted that she had what she needed and was glad she trusted V.
Before leaving for the Crystal Palace job, V stopped at the Afterlife bar and had a drink with Claire, who was tending the bar.
In the Temperance epilogue Judy sent V a run of texts repeatedly asking V to pick up the phone, ending with a worried "V? Hello?".
In the Temperance epilogue River sent V a run of texts begging V to pick up and saying he was turning Night City upside down trying to find V.
In the 2079 holocall Judy told V she was living in Pittsburgh and had gotten married, and that she could not help V.
In the 2079 holocall River told V he had needed money for Randy's rehab, so he did a deal with Trauma Team and sold them police secrets.
T-Bug's connection failed during the Konpeki lockdown while V and Jackie were escaping.
Jackie supported V after Arasaka revoked V's corporate status at Lizzie's. They already knew each other; this was not their first meeting.
V and Jackie recovered Sandra Dorsett and transferred her alive to Trauma Team, with T-Bug supporting the extraction.
V and Jackie obtained the Flathead for Dex's heist job.
V compromised the parade float's system at the Arasaka industrial park and withdrew, completing that part of Takemura's plan.
Takemura forcibly abducted Hanako from the parade, and V escaped the ensuing pursuit.
In the safe house, Hanako heard V say they witnessed Saburo's death and accuse Yorinobu of the murder. Takemura was present.
Dex promised a forty percent heist cut as a bonus for V's honesty about Evelyn. Jackie attended the briefing. This was not payment received.
Dex promised a thirty-five percent cut for the heist during the briefing Jackie attended. This was a promise, not payment received.
Takemura told V that Arasaka took Jackie's body and could extract a damaged, incomplete engram with Soulkiller. Takemura admitted he understood little of the method.
Delamain confirmed that Jackie’s body was delivered to his family, and Mama Welles later held his ofrenda.
Mama Welles knew Jackie had died and mourned him.
V and Jackie witnessed Yorinobu kill Saburo while hiding in the Konpeki penthouse.
V killed Oda at the parade despite Takemura's appeal for mercy.
Oda refused to help V and Takemura after the secret meeting and warned them about pursuing Hanako.
Jackie supported V after Arasaka revoked V's corporate status at Lizzie's. They already knew each other; this was not their first meeting.
V and Jackie escaped the failed border smuggling run together and agreed to help each other in Night City.
V and Jackie survived their rival attempt to steal the car and began their partnership after the police released them.
V cleared the parade sniper route and reached the netrunner's access point while supporting Takemura.
V and Jackie escaped the hostile Maelstrom factory after the negotiation broke down.
V and Jackie survived the Militech assault inside All Foods and completed the factory escape.
V and Jackie finished the Flathead transaction and left All Foods through the peaceful factory route.
Anthony Gilchrist met V and Jackie after the factory job.
Meredith Stout met V and Jackie outside All Foods after the factory job.
During the briefing, V told Dex about Evelyn's proposal to cut him out. Jackie and T-Bug heard the disclosure.
V and Jackie recovered Sandra Dorsett and transferred her alive to Trauma Team, with T-Bug supporting the extraction.
V incapacitated Royce with the physical takedown during the negotiations. This receipt does not establish his eventual survival or later Maelstrom leadership.
V shot and killed Royce during the Flathead negotiations. Jackie was present.
V interrupted the negotiations with a direct attack on Royce: a shooting or physical takedown.
V offered Royce a Militech-chip payment after warning him about the malware or saying it had been removed.
V handed Royce the compromised Militech chip without warning him about its malware.
V paid Royce for the Flathead with personal funds during the deal Jackie attended.
V and Jackie witnessed Yorinobu kill Saburo while hiding in the Konpeki penthouse.
V and Takemura began cooperating after their diner conversation about Saburo's murder and the Relic predicament.
V escaped the safe-house assault without bringing Takemura out. The resulting story branch treats Takemura as lost; Johnny had urged V to leave.
V returned upstairs for Takemura during the safe-house assault, and they both escaped.
V declined joining the industrial-park reconnaissance, leaving Takemura to scout alone.
V joined Takemura for reconnaissance of the Arasaka industrial park.
Takemura recovered V from the landfill after killing Dex. V and Takemura survived the pursuing Arasaka attackers together and sought medical help.
V accepted the shared van ride with Takemura to Jig-Jig Street.
V took Fiona Vargas' controlled leak instead of her full client data; Hands passed it to the client but complained the roster was shorter than expected and lacked heavier hitters.
V refused Fiona Vargas' offer and took her full client data; Hands' debrief said the Europeans could now make sure the tax evaders were punished.
V texted Hands that the client had been stuck believing he was someone else after a BD accident, and that V had helped him back to his old self.
During the BD shoot V directed, V handed Tool his own fan letter as his lines; it brought Edgar Tool back to himself, ruining the scroll Lina Malina had expected to film.
V texted Hands that the client was really Tool, a BD-rental owner who believed he was Lina Malina, and that after V freed him he now thought he was an FIA clone.
During the BD shoot V directed, V convinced Tool that he was a clone created by the FIA. It was a script for the shoot, not a fact about Tool.
V texted Hands that the "Lina Malina" client was really Tool, a BD-rental owner locked in the basement by his business partner, and that V had simply set him free.
To get Lina Malina to the BD shoot, V transferred her the advance she demanded by text and sent her the Brainporium address.
V texted Hands that the "kidnapped Lina Malina" gig was really about Edgar Tool, who believed he was Lina, and that V had convinced him he was her sister.
During the BD shoot V directed, V convinced Tool he was Lina Malina's long-lost sister; the TooLina scroll worked, and Lina later messaged V that it was exactly what her brand needed.
Some time after V got him out of Dodger's den, Bill Mitchell messaged V that he had laid down his badge to open a business of his own in the Glen.
V's Heaviest of Hearts job turned into a fight inside Heavy Hearts, Hands' own club; his debrief chided V for making such a mess there.
In Heaviest of Hearts, V had the forged testimony against Michael Maldonado deleted outright; Hands reported that Maldonado had nothing but praise for V.
V ended Spy in the Jungle by leaving Mark Bana's biomonitor at Hands' drop point, as Steven Santos had urged, instead of giving it to Ana; Hands approved of V's "good sense".
V followed Steven Santos' request and left Mark Bana's biomonitor at the fixer's drop point instead of giving it to Ana; Steven later reached out to V, grateful for V's part in it.
When V met Ana Friedman and Steven Santos at the end of Spy in the Jungle, V destroyed Mark Bana's biomonitor in front of them instead of handing it over.
At the end of Spy in the Jungle, V handed Mark Bana's biomonitor over to the agents for Ana Friedman to use, rather than suppressing it as Steven Santos had asked.
After Spy in the Jungle, Hands noted that Mark Bana's fate was all over the news once the biomonitor reached the agents, and that what mattered to him was that they had been paid.
Once V had finished every job Hands had in Dogtown, he invited V to Heavy Hearts for a reward and a proper goodbye, and V met him there to collect it.
In Prototype in the Scraper, V talked Hands into having a chrome-doc recover the Zetatech implant from Hasan Demir and letting Hasan go free instead of handing him back to Zetatech; Hands agreed.
In Roads to Redemption, V got into the stadium weapons factory and uploaded Nele's software to the Crimson Harvest Net-nuke, disarming it before it could be used.
The Haven clinic confrontation in Dogtown Saints ended with Anthony Anderson killed by Nika; Hands' debrief acknowledged Anderson's death while noting the scavengers had been cleared out.
Hands closed V's Dogtown Saints gig as premium work: the scavengers were dealt with and Anthony Anderson came out of it alive.
In Shot by Both Sides, V sided with Bree Whitney: the objective to kill Dante was completed, and Hands then told V the client was pleased and paid.
Hands warned V by holocall that Bree Whitney had sold Militech's data to NetWatch and vanished, and that NetWatch had dispatched a hunter in the aftermath.
As promised for Yoko's help, V texted Mr. Hands the coordinates of Reed's convoy ambush site, the road by the abandoned hotel on Pacifica Blvd.

After Treating Symptoms, Alan Noël messaged V that the NetWatch operation had paid off: Milko led them to the man behind the Voodoo Boys' old Militech bots, a Belgrade arms dealer selling them to separatists.
In Treating Symptoms, V agreed to let Alan Noël finish his NetWatch operation and left Milko Alexis alive instead of carrying out the hit.
V closed the Treating Symptoms gig without killing Milko Alexis; Hands' debrief said his NetWatch contacts put the client, Indira Barazza, under round-the-clock netrunner protection instead.
After Run This Town, Hands messaged V that, by some miracle, Jago and Bennett were working in tandem and Dogtown had never been this well run.
After Run This Town, Hands messaged V that Jago was dead and gone and that Bennett now ran Dogtown on his own.
After Run This Town, Hands messaged V that Jago, Dogtown's new top dog, had stopped by his office for tea to discuss business.
After Run This Town, Hands messaged V that Bennett was no longer missed and that Jago was running Dogtown better than expected.
After Angie's withdrawal, V advised Aaron to throw the bout as the safer choice. This advice alone does not establish what later happened in the ring or to his career.
After Angie's withdrawal, V encouraged Aaron to fight honestly instead of deliberately losing. The advice does not itself guarantee victory or safety.

V has disclosed accepting Angie's arrangement while Aaron was unconscious at the clinic. Aaron did not witness the negotiation itself; this establishes the agreement, not that the later bout has already happened.
V has disclosed driving Angie away at the clinic with a threat invoking Sasquatch. Aaron was unconscious during that exchange and cannot quote it as firsthand experience.

Aaron reported throwing the match, then leaving competitive boxing and finding satisfying work coaching young people in Dogtown. These are his actual later reports in this save, not a prediction from V's earlier advice.
Aaron reported losing the honest bout by knockout in the tenth round. In a later message he said he had reached Costa Rica and was earning money in street fights on a path he chose himself.

During the completed farewell, this save records V giving Alex the presidential coin. She accepted the keepsake. This does not establish a romance, a later postcard, or a separate decision to retain the coin.

V completed a later private farewell with the living Alex at the Moth. Alex disclosed that her last assignment was to eliminate V, but said she was content to let the Relic illness take its course. This encounter does not establish that V has died or that Alex has already retired.

This save records V meeting Alex at the Moth with Reed and completing their discussion. Alex learned that Reed was still alive. This establishes their operational first contact, without implying later friendship or romance.
This save records that Songbird survived Cynosure and V completed the border handover to NUSA custody with Reed. Her later condition and recovery are not established by that transfer.
This save records that Songbird was dead at Cynosure and V completed delivery of her body to the NUSA at the border with Reed. This observation does not reveal the private cause or her last request.
V has told Reed that V accepted the medal Myers offered after returning Songbird alive. Acceptance of the object does not prove political loyalty, gratitude, or agreement with Myers.
At the Cynosure core, V refused Songbird's request to die and kept her alive. The later NUSA handover and any operation on V remain separate events.
V complied with Songbird's request to die at the Cynosure core. This is the canonical saved outcome, disclosed by V to this listener; a spawned copy does not undo the death.
At the conclusion of the Cynosure core scene, Reed arrived to find Songbird dead. This observation does not make him an eyewitness to her preceding private exchange with V.

The saved stadium outcome records Alex's death during the ICEbreaker branch. A managed Alex copy does not change that canonical outcome. This account is available here only after V has disclosed it to this listener.
The saved story records V attempting to incapacitate Songbird during the stadium lab operation. Songbird directly experienced the attempted capture.
The saved story records V helping Songbird through the stadium lab operation.

The saved NCX aftermath records an accepted arrangement for Reed to help secure treatment for V. The agreement may have been accepted after the confrontation by message. It establishes neither a completed operation nor its result.

The NCX sequence ended with Reed taking Songbird alive into FIA custody. This evidence does not identify whether V explicitly handed her over or withdrew, and does not by itself establish a cure agreement.

The NCX launchpad sequence ended with Reed dead and Songbird sent away on the lunar shuttle. Johnny witnessed and discussed this outcome. Her subsequent medical recovery is not established by the launch.

V has disclosed that Reed died at NCX and Songbird left aboard the lunar shuttle. Songbird was unconscious for the confrontation, and neither she nor Alex receives Reed's exact last exchange as firsthand memory.
The completed gig records Nele being taken into Biotechnica custody. The evidence does not distinguish explicit surrender from V withdrawing, and does not reveal her later fate.
V has disclosed that Nele was taken into Biotechnica custody after the gig. The exact surrender or withdrawal sequence and her subsequent fate remain unconfirmed.
V defeated the corporate team, spoke with Nele afterward, and let her leave. This outcome does not establish that the attackers all died or that the farewell was friendly.
This save records that V accepted the FIA treatment arrangement with Reed and boarded the FIA transport for treatment. The operation and its eventual outcome are not yet established by these records.
This save records that V accepted the FIA treatment arrangement with Reed and boarded the FIA transport for treatment. The operation and its eventual outcome are not yet established by these records.
Reed privately explained the ICEbreaker that Farida would install to incapacitate Songbird. This establishes Reed's plan and V's briefing, not that V ultimately chose to use it.

Reed privately explained the ICEbreaker that Farida would install to incapacitate Songbird. This establishes Reed's plan and V's briefing, not that V ultimately chose to use it. Songbird can recount this only after V discloses it; she did not witness the private decision.

In the completed private meeting, Songbird told V that she helped Hansen spring the trap on Myers in exchange for the neural matrix. She said she expected the plane to be grounded and Myers delivered, rather than destroyed and hunted down. This remains her account.

V experienced multiple subjective fragments of Songbird's past in Cynosure, including her Brooklyn life, ties to Reed and Myers, and the Blackwall's effect on her. They are not a complete independent record of every event, and Songbird may discuss V's perception only after V tells her.

Songbird supplied a lead placing her at the Black Sapphire, and V relayed that location to Reed after the Slider encounter. This is the lead received at that time, not a claim that she remains there later.
This save records V directly communicating with Songbird and agreeing to her proposed bargain after their first conversation.
During the recorded first-contact bargain, Songbird promised that she could cure V. This was her offer; these receipts do not establish an available treatment or a cure for both of them.

After Songbird's lunar shuttle departure, V found and looted the Songbird cache associated with her later recording. Its presence suggests a follow-up from Songbird, but does not establish her current medical condition or the exact sender's actions.
V downloaded the optional Blind_n_Dead file from the twins' data and obtained a stash lead. Reed may use the file detail only after V discloses that optional find.

coWitnesses.origin: experienced it through V's eyes as the engram in V's head; not physically present
coWitnesses.rationale: From the Relic's activation after The Heist until Mikoshi, Johnny's engram shares V's senses and comments on what V sees, hears and does, including private conversations and romance. He therefore knows V-involved outcomes that other reviewed rules establish for other speakers. Excluded: the prologue and Heist (before the engram was active), Playing for Time (it surfaces only at its end), and the Devil, Star, Sun and 2079 epilogues, where Johnny is no longer with V. Temperance is kept because Johnny lives it. Rules still need their own native predicate and V as a recipient; group speech still requires every other listener to be a declared recipient.
